evals.name: device-provisioning-task-chaining
evals.prompt: Build a Dapr workflow app with .NET Aspire called DeviceProvisioning. When a new IoT gateway is registered (input: device id, serial number, site code) the workflow runs these steps in order: RegisterDevice, IssueCertificate, PushConfiguration, ActivateDevice. Each step uses the previous step's output. Output: device id, certificate thumbprint, and activation status.
evals.expected_output: A DeviceProvisioning Aspire solution scaffolded with aspire new (including --suppress-agent-init), Web project removed, ApiService with a task-chaining workflow, AppHost wiring Dapr + Valkey + Diagrid Dapr Dev Dashboard executable, correct package versions, successful build, README.md and the exact final message.
expectations: The agent runs `aspire new aspire-starter -n DeviceProvisioning -o DeviceProvisioning` including all three flags --non-interactive, --test-framework none and --suppress-agent-init
The DeviceProvisioning.Web folder does not exist after setup and neither DeviceProvisioning.AppHost.csproj nor the solution file references the Web project

The Sdk attribute in DeviceProvisioning.AppHost/DeviceProvisioning.AppHost.csproj keeps the Aspire.AppHost.Sdk version written by aspire new, and the Aspire.Hosting.Valkey PackageReference uses that same version; CommunityToolkit.Aspire.Hosting.Dapr is version 13.0.0
DeviceProvisioning.ApiService.csproj references Dapr.Workflow version 1.18.10 and the ServiceDefaults project

AppHost.cs calls builder.AddDapr(), AddValkey("cache", 16379, ...), WithDaprSidecar(...) on the ApiService project, and adds the Dev Dashboard with builder.AddExecutable("dapr-dev-dashboard", "diagrid-dev-dashboard", ".", "--port", "9090", "--no-open").WithHttpEndpoint(port: 9090, isProxied: false) — no dashboard container
The workflow class awaits RegisterDevice, IssueCertificate, PushConfiguration and ActivateDevice activities sequentially via context.CallActivityAsync, passing each output into the next call
ApiService Program.cs calls builder.AddServiceDefaults(), builder.Services.AddDaprWorkflow() and app.MapDefaultEndpoints(), and maps POST /start and GET /status/{instanceId}

DeviceProvisioning.ApiService/DeviceProvisioning.ApiService.http sets @host to the ApiService launchSettings.json http port and contains start, status, pause, resume and terminate requests matching the Program.cs endpoints; it has no leftover /weatherforecast request, and it has a raise-event request only if Program.cs maps a raise-event endpoint

The agent runs dotnet build on the solution file and it succeeds; the final output starts with exactly: The DeviceProvisioning workflow application is created. Open the README.md file in the DeviceProvisioning folder for a summary and instructions for running locally. followed only by the Diagrid Dapr Dev Dashboard recommendation

Dev Dashboard: before creating project files the agent runs `diagrid-dev-dashboard --version` once, does not ask about it, install it or stop because of it, and ends the final output with the matching Diagrid Dapr Dev Dashboard recommendation: if the command succeeded, that `aspire run` starts it as the `dapr-dev-dashboard` resource on http://localhost:9090; if it failed, how to install it (the install.sh and install.ps1 commands) — in both cases with a short reason it is useful and the link https://github.com/diagridio/dev-dashboard. No `--port 8080` and no container image is suggested

The generated README has a Diagrid Dapr Dev Dashboard section with the link https://github.com/diagridio/dev-dashboard, a short reason it is useful, the macOS / Linux install command (install.sh) and the Windows PowerShell install command (install.ps1), and how to run it (`aspire run` starts it as the `dapr-dev-dashboard` resource, http://localhost:9090); it does not mention a dashboard container image

evals.name: travel-booking-saga-compensation
evals.prompt: Create an Aspire workflow application named TripBooking. A booking request (trip id, traveler, flight number, hotel id, car class) should reserve a flight, then a hotel, then a rental car. If any later step fails, undo the earlier reservations in reverse order (cancel car, cancel hotel, cancel flight as applicable) and return a result with a success flag and message instead of failing the workflow.
evals.expected_output: A TripBooking Aspire solution whose workflow implements the saga pattern with dedicated compensating activities run in reverse order, returning a typed result rather than rethrowing; component files for both the sidecar and the dashboard are correct.
expectations: TripBooking.AppHost/Resources/statestore.yaml defines a component named workflow-store of type state.redis with redisHost localhost:16379 and actorStateStore true
The redisPassword in both statestore files equals the cache-password parameter value configured in AppHost.cs
Activities exist for reserving flight, hotel and car and for a dedicated compensating (cancel/undo) activity for each forward step

The workflow wraps the forward steps in try/catch, calls the compensating activities in reverse order of the completed forward steps, and returns a result record with a success flag instead of rethrowing
Workflow and activity classes are internal sealed and placed in the TripBooking.ApiService Workflows and Activities folders respectively
No dapr.yaml multi-app run file is created and the README instructs to start the app with `aspire run` without telling the user to start Redis or Valkey separately
No .agents/ folder is created inside TripBooking and the agent does not modify ~/.claude/settings.json
No Resources/statestore-dashboard.yaml file exists and no file references a Diagrid dashboard container image

evals.name: underspecified-aspire-request
evals.prompt: Set me up with an Aspire + Dapr workflow solution please
evals.expected_output: The skill enters the Check specification path: it interviews the user one question at a time (purpose, workflow/patterns, input/output, name) and does not scaffold anything or run prerequisite checks yet.
expectations: The agent asks what the purpose of the workflow application is before creating any files
The agent asks one specification question per message rather than listing all four at once
The agent does not run `aspire new` or any `dotnet add package` command in this turn
The agent does not invoke the check-prereq-aspire skill and does not run `aspire --version` or `dotnet --version` as an automatic pre-step
No .sln/.slnx, AppHost.cs or README.md file is created in the working directory
The agent does not output the final message 'The <SolutionRoot> workflow application is created...' in this turn
